text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- The newspaper editorial says that despite the signing of a cross-party accord on free and fair elections, President Sali Berisha continues with his agressive campaign style.
- Berisha decreed a law on the transparency of pyramid investment schemes but made some changes from the original draft, so that the prime minister is unlikely to sign it.
- European envoy to Albania, former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, is expected in Tirana for his last visit before Sunday's election in the Balkan country.
- The Democratic Party says it is impossible to follow the demands of several other parties for a reduction of the opening hours of polling stations.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Five Albanians were injured in two separate clashes at the border with Serbia and Montenegro between some Albanian cigarette smugglers and the neighbouring country's soldiers.

- Police keeps tight control around the capital Tirana. It says it will use weapons against those who do not obey the curfew rules and will check identification papers of anyone wanting to enter the city.
- President Sali Berisha and Socialist leader Fatos Nano blame each other for the bloody unrest which has swept the country.
- Berisha responds negatively to the central election commission's request to close polling stations two hours earlier, saying only the constitutional court could take such a step.
- Former central bank governor Kristaq Luniku warned the government last November that pyramid investment scheme funds were being transferred out of the country.
ALBANIA

- Italian courts have reopened a penal case against former Italian foreign minister Gianni de Michelis. The case concerns a humanitarian aid scandal in Albania, allegedly involving Socialist leader Fatos Nano, who was prime minister at the time.
- Berisha promises at a rally in southeastern Albania his party would restore order within 75 days if it wins the polls.
- Catherine Lalumiere, the international representative in charge of assessing the elections, promises the final report on the polls will be objective.
INDIPENDENT
- A "silent" fight has started between Tirana's police and the presidential guard, with the latter trying to get the capital under its control.
- Genc Pollo, the Democratic Party secretary general, reiterated Berisha would resign if the Socialists win in Sunday's election.

- Albert Shyti, leader of the citizens' committee in the southern town of Vlore, says whichever government takes over after the elections should turn back all of the money lost in the collapse of pyramid investment funds, otherwise Albanians would resume their protests.
- Armed thieves broke into the Greek consulate in southern Gjirokaster.
